However, the consistent 07:30 departure makes this less likely than the standard worker hypothesis. This hypothesis remains viable if the resident works from home but leaves for errands/coffee at that time.

The consistent early morning departure (07:30) on both observed days makes a standard night shift highly unlikely. The late evening presence (21:38-21:45) is more indicative of leisure or late work than a shift start. Probability reduced due to lack of contradictory evidence for standard work hours.
